root_cause.text: The driver incorrectly used WARN_ON (which triggers kernel warnings or panics) to validate non-critical ACPI object types and buffer lengths, causing frequent spurious warnings that degrade system stability when firmware does not meet expected formats.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces WARN_ON(obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER) and similar checks with simple if conditions, removing the kernel warnings. The commit message states these WARN_ONs "trigger a lot" and are "most likely harmless," indicating the conditions are not actual security or functional errors. The Fixes commit introduced these WARN_ONs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove overly cautious WARN_ON checks from ACPI GSP capability validation, silently handling invalid objects instead of triggering kernel warnings.
intent_record.what: Removed WARN_ON() macro invocations from two conditional checks that validate ACPI object type and buffer length, keeping the same logical conditions.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when obj->type is not ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER or its buffer length is not 4, the code will no longer emit a kernel warning (via WARN_ON) before jumping to the 'done' label; it will silently skip the capability update.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary kernel warnings that can be triggered by expected or benign conditions.
intent_record.what: Removed WARN_ON() macros from two conditional checks, leaving only the type and length comparisons.
intent_record.how: Previously, a kernel warning was triggered if the ACPI object type was not a buffer or its length was not 4. Now, those conditions cause the function to jump to 'done' without emitting a warning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove WARN_ON from DOD validity checks to suppress unnecessary kernel warnings when encountering invalid ACPI _DOD packages.
intent_record.what: Removed two WARN_ON macro invocations from the conditional checks in r535_gsp_acpi_dod(). The conditions themselves remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: Previously, when either condition (invalid type or count exceeding array size) was true, a kernel warning (with backtrace) would be printed before early return. Now the function returns early silently without emitting any warning.
